lesson.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI, Pydantic and Uvicorn
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Build a REST API with FastAPI, Pydantic and Uvicorn

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, then create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and an `@app.get("/")` route returning {"Hello": "World"}. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open http://127.0.0.1:8000 to see the JSON.

targets.caption: Create the FastAPI app instance
Decorator defining the GET route for the root path
Server is up at http://127.0.0.1:8000
The JSON returned by the root route

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server that runs FastAPI apps
The @app.get decorator defines a path for HTTP GET
uvicorn main:app means file name : app variable
--reload restarts the server on file changes

hints: Install both packages first: pip install fastapi uvicorn.
In main.py, import FastAPI, create app = FastAPI(), then decorate a function with @app.get("/") that returns a dict.
Run uvicorn from the folder that contains main.py: uvicorn main:app --reload.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in the browser. You should see {"Hello":"World"}.
common_mistakes: Installing fastapi but not uvicorn, so the uvicorn command is not found.
Running uvicorn from a different directory than main.py, which gives 'Could not import module "main"'.
Mismatching the app name, e.g. naming it api = FastAPI() but running main:app ('Attribute "app" not found').
Forgetting the parentheses in FastAPI() or the leading slash in @app.get("/").
Typing uvicorn main.py:app instead of uvicorn main:app.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: In main.py add a module-level `items = []` list and an `@app.post("/items")` function `create_item(item: str)` that appends the item and returns the list. With uvicorn running, test it with `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'`.

targets.caption: Module-level list that stores the items
POST endpoint at the /items path
Send a POST request with the item as a query parameter

explanations.topic: What routes are in FastAPI
Using a POST request to create items
A function argument becomes a query parameter
Passing a query parameter in the curl URL

hints: Create an empty list named items above your routes, then add a function decorated with @app.post("/items").
Give the function one parameter, item: str. FastAPI reads it from the query string.
Inside the function, call items.append(item) and then return items.
Keep uvicorn running. In a second terminal run: curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'
common_mistakes: Using @app.get instead of @app.post, so the curl -X POST call returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Defining items = [] inside the function, which resets the list on every request.
Leaving out ?item=... in the URL, which returns a 422 'field required' error.
Leaving the URL unquoted in the shell, so the ? or & is interpreted by the shell.
Running curl in the same terminal as uvicorn instead of opening a new one.
Forgetting to save main.py, or running without --reload, so the new route isn't picked up.

steps.title: Add GET endpoint by item ID
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with `get_item(item_id: int)` returning `items[item_id]`. After the reload, re-add items with the POST curl, then run `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0`.

targets.caption: New endpoint with a path parameter in curly braces
Type hint lets FastAPI convert the path value to int
Fetching index 0 returns the first item

explanations.topic: Path parameters: {item_id} in the route becomes a function argument
Auto-reload resets the in-memory items list, so re-add items before testing
Path value maps to the same-named function parameter
Type hints make FastAPI convert the path string to int

hints: Use the same @app.get decorator as before, but put the variable part of the path in curly braces.
The name inside the braces must match a parameter of your function, e.g. item_id.
Annotate the parameter as int so it can index the list: def get_item(item_id: int).
After saving, the server reloads and the list is empty: POST an item again, then curl /items/0.
common_mistakes: Testing right after saving without re-adding items, so items[0] raises IndexError (500 Internal Server Error).
Leaving out the int type hint, so item_id is a str and indexing the list fails.
Parameter name not matching the {item_id} placeholder in the path.
Using an index past the end of the list (e.g. /items/3 with two items), which gives a 500 error until the 404 handling is added in the next step.

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: In main.py import `HTTPException` from fastapi and make get_item return the item if `item_id < len(items)`, otherwise `raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")`. Request a missing index with curl (e.g. /items/7) to see the 404 detail.

targets.caption: Import HTTPException from fastapi
Raise a 404 when the item doesn't exist
The curl response now shows a helpful 404 detail

explanations.topic: Why an internal server error is unhelpful for a missing item
HTTP status codes: a missing item is a 4xx client error
404 Not Found as the right response
The detail parameter adds context to the error

hints: Before returning the item, check whether the requested index actually exists in your list.
Compare item_id against len(items): return the item if it's in range, otherwise raise an error.
Add HTTPException to your fastapi import, then use: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")
Make sure uvicorn reloaded (run with --reload), then curl an index larger than your list to see {"detail": ...}.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import HTTPException from fastapi, causing a NameError
Using return HTTPException(...) instead of raise, which won't produce a 404
Using <= instead of < in the bounds check, so the last index+1 still raises IndexError
Not restarting uvicorn (or not using --reload), so the old 500 error persists
Requesting an index that does exist, so no 404 is shown

steps.title: List items with limit parameter
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items")` with `list_items(limit: int = 10)` returning `items[0:limit]`. Add several items, then test with `curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'`.

targets.caption: New list_items endpoint with a typed limit query parameter
Request with limit=3 returns only the first 3 items

explanations.topic: Query parameters and automatic type conversion (str to int)
limit slices the list; default 10 used when omitted
Same path, different HTTP method routes to a different function
Default value defined in the function header

hints: Add a new function decorated with @app.get on the same "/items" path you used for POST.
Give the function a parameter limit typed as int with a default of 10. FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Return a slice of your list: items[0:limit].
POST a few items first, then run curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3' and check that you get exactly 3 back.
common_mistakes: Using @app.post instead of @app.get, so the GET request returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Leaving off the int type hint, so limit stays a string and slicing raises a TypeError (500 error).
Forgetting to quote the URL in curl, which lets the shell interpret ? or &.
Testing before adding any items: the list is empty, so you get [] back.
Not restarting uvicorn (or not running with --reload), so the new endpoint isn't loaded. Restarting also clears the in-memory list, so add items again before testing.

steps.title: Use a Pydantic Item model
steps.instructions: In main.py import `BaseModel` from pydantic, define `class Item(BaseModel)` with `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, and make create_item take `item: Item`. POST JSON with curl, then confirm a body without `text` fails validation.

targets.caption: Import BaseModel from Pydantic
The Item model with text and is_done
create_item now takes an Item from the JSON body
Response is now an Item object, with is_done defaulting to false

explanations.topic: Why Pydantic models: structure, validation, docs, IDE completion
Model arguments are read from the JSON body, not the query string
Default values: is_done falls back to false
Removing the default makes a field required and validated

hints: Start with `from pydantic import BaseModel`, then write a class that inherits from it, with typed attributes.
Your fields are `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`. Change create_item's parameter to `item: Item` and add `-> Item` to get_item.
The old `?item=apple` query string won't work any more. Send JSON instead: curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"apple"}' 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items'
To see validation, remove any default on `text`, restart or let --reload pick it up, then post `{"title":"apple"}`. You should get a 422 error naming the missing `text` field.
common_mistakes: Still sending the item as a `?item=` query parameter. With a model argument, FastAPI expects a JSON body and returns 422.
Leaving out `-H 'Content-Type: application/json'`, or using shell quoting that mangles the JSON body.
Writing `class Item:` without `(BaseModel)`, so FastAPI doesn't treat it as a request body model.
Giving `text` a default value. Then a body without `text` is accepted instead of failing validation.
Not restarting uvicorn (or not running it with --reload), so the old string-based endpoint is still being served.
Annotating `is_done` as `str` or `boolean` instead of Python's `bool`.

steps.title: Add response models to endpoints
steps.instructions: In main.py, add `response_model=list[Item]` to the list_items decorator and `response_model=Item` to the get_item decorator. Let uvicorn reload and re-run the GET requests to confirm the responses match the model.

targets.caption: Declare that get_item returns an Item
Declare that list_items returns a list of Items

explanations.topic: Modeling responses with the same Pydantic BaseModel used for requests
response_model argument on the route decorator
Response models tell clients the shape of the endpoint's output

hints: The change goes in the route decorators, not in the function bodies.
Add a keyword argument named response_model to @app.get(...) for each endpoint.
For a single item use response_model=Item; for the list endpoint wrap it: response_model=list[Item].
Save the file so uvicorn --reload restarts, then repeat your GET requests (curl or /docs).
common_mistakes: Writing response_model=Item on the list endpoint, which fails validation because a list is returned.
Putting response_model as a function parameter instead of a decorator argument.
Using list[Item] on Python < 3.9 without importing List from typing.
Passing an instance like Item() instead of the class Item.
Forgetting to save, so the reloaded server still runs the old code.

steps.title: Explore the interactive docs
steps.instructions: With uvicorn main:app --reload running, open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, expand POST /items, click Try it out and Execute with a JSON body. Also visit /redoc and /openapi.json to see the generated schema.

targets.caption: Expand the POST /items endpoint in Swagger UI
Click Try it out, edit the request body, then Execute
The real response from your server appears here
Small link under the title opens the raw OpenAPI schema
Uvicorn logs each request you execute

explanations.topic: FastAPI auto-generates interactive documentation for free
Swagger UI at /docs lists endpoints, methods and parameters
Execute shows the equivalent curl command and sends a real request
/redoc is an alternative documentation view
openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses, useful for building clients

hints: Make sure your uvicorn server is still running in the terminal, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in the browser.
Click the POST /items row to expand it, then press the 'Try it out' button at its top right.
Edit the example JSON in the request body to match your Item model's fields, then click Execute and scroll down to 'Response body'.
Change the path to /redoc to see the alternative docs, and click the small /openapi.json link under the title to see the raw schema.
common_mistakes: Opening /docs while the uvicorn server is stopped, so the browser shows 'This site can't be reached'.
Clicking Execute without pressing 'Try it out' first, so the request body stays read-only.
Sending a request body with missing or wrongly typed fields, which returns a 422 Unprocessable Entity response.
Typing /doc or /docs/ with a typo, which gives a 404 Not Found instead of the Swagger UI.
Using localhost on a different port than the one uvicorn printed.
